en: A state that is neither a cause nor internal is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is a cause and internal. (Abbreviated. Nine [ways] in the case of the object; nine in the case of predominance and decisive support; three in the cases of prenascence, presence, and non-disappearance.

A state that is neither a cause nor external is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is a cause and external. (Abbreviated. Nine [ways] in the case of the object; nine in the case of predominance and decisive support;
three in the cases of prenascence, presence, and non-disappearance. (The "Internal Triplet" is not found in the sections beginning with the "Dependent" Chapter.)
